Addition of a taxane (docetaxel or paclitaxel) to an anthra- cycline-based regimen appears to improve disease-free and overall survival.21,22 There is evidence that HER2-re- ceptor status is prognostic for response to anthracycline- based regimens.3 There is also increasing interest in the early use of trastuzumab in women with HER2-overex- pressing tumours. Studies of adjuvant trastuzumab have shown significant improvements in disease-free survival and overall survival,3,23-26 although there are concerns about cardiotoxicity.27 The benefits of trastuzumab are in- dependent of ER status.3 Reducing dose intensity of chemotherapy results in poorer survival, and this has led to the hypothesis that higher dos- es may offer more benefit, particularly in patients at high risk of recurrence. However, despite some positive reports of high-dose chemotherapy with stem-cell support, ran- domised studies have largely failed to show any benefit of high-dose over standard-dose therapy.28,29 The results of the analyses above established 5 years of tamoxifen as the standard of care for adjuvant hormonal therapy in ER-positive disease (it is now accepted that it should not be given to women with ER-negative tu- mours,1,3,9 in whom it is of little value). However, some guidelines now suggest that aromatase inhibitors should be substituted for, or added to, tamoxifen, in postmenopausal women with ER-positive disease,3,30 an area that is still be- ing intensively studied.31 There is evidence that 5 years of anastrozole is an effective alternative to tamoxifen,31,32 and 2 years of treatment with letrozole was found to fur- ther reduce the risk of recurrence compared with tamoxifen.33 Two to 3 years of tamoxifen followed by an aromatase inhibitor (anastrozole, exemestane, or letrozole) has also been investigated and appears promising.31,34-36 In addition, although extending tamoxifen beyond 5 years is not advocated, there may be significant benefits to follow- ing a full course of tamoxifen with extended therapy with an aromatase inhibitor;31 the optimum length of such ther- apy has yet to be determined.
